key_insight: NeuronSoup evolves asynchronous, shared-neuron temporal graphs that compute via delay-mediated signal propagation and neuron state interference, without backpropagation.
engineering_relevance: It offers a compact alternative neural architecture that can adapt computation depth per sample and potentially discover useful lateral interactions not hard-coded in standard deep networks.
method: Routes continuous signals through variable-length paths from input to output.
Shares hidden neurons across paths so later arrivals interact with residual state.
Uses a genetic algorithm to co-evolve topology, weights, delays, and connectivity on a flat real-valued genome.
evidence_signal: On frozen ResNet18 features for MNIST, the evolved system reached 85.9% test accuracy with 204 active paths, 266 hidden neurons, and a 115 KB model after 10,000 generations.
watch_item: The approach is highly optimization-dependent and may be difficult to scale or reproduce outside the specific feature-extraction and evolutionary setup.
paper_title: NeuronSoup: Evolving Asynchronous, Shared-Neuron Temporal Graphs without Backpropagation
